summary.title: University Digital Library Management System
summary.description: The University Digital Library is a web app where students and teachers search and download digital books and papers, librarians manage the content, and admins control accounts and permissions. It uses a cloud database and requires login for all users. The aim is secure, role-based access with no unauthorized access, tampering, or service disruption.

diagrams.title: New STRIDE diagram

data.name: Users / Internet
data.description: Untrusted zone. All users connect from here. Needs HTTPS and authentication.

data.name: Application Server
data.description: Semi-trusted zone. Business logic runs here. Needs input validation and access control.

data.name: Student
data.description: Searches, views, and downloads library resources. Read-only access.

data.name: Teacher
data.description: Searches, views, and downloads resources. Same as student but may access licensed content.

data.name: Administrator
data.description: Creates, updates, deletes user accounts and assigns roles. Highest privilege.

data.name: Librarian
data.description: Adds, edits, and removes books/papers. Write access to resource database.

threats.title: Stolen session token used to upload fake resources.
threats.description: An attacker steals a Librarian's active session cookie via cross-site scripting (XSS). They use the stolen session to upload malicious PDF files to the library without needing the Librarian's password.
threats.mitigation: Implement short session timeouts, use HttpOnly and Secure flags on cookies, and enforce re-authentication for upload actions.

data.name:
1.0 
Authenticate
User
data.description: Verifies username/password against User Accounts DB and assigns role. Handles credentials

threats.title: Attacker guesses a Teacher's password
threats.description: An external attacker uses an automated brute-force tool against the login process. Because there is no limit on failed attempts, they eventually guess a teacher's password and gain unauthorized access to download restricted academic papers.
threats.mitigation: Lock the account after 5 failed attempts, enforce rate limiting, and require 12-character passwords with MFA for teachers.

data.name:
2.0 
Search 
& 
Retrieve 
Resources
data.description: Handles search queries and returns matching books/papers from resources DB.

threats.title: Botnet floods the search function
threats.description: An attacker uses a botnet to send thousands of automated search queries per second to Process 2.0. The application server becomes overloaded and crashes, preventing legitimate students from searching for resources.
threats.mitigation: Implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) and API rate limiting to block high-volume traffic from single IP addresses.

data.name:
3.0 
Manage 
Resources
data.description: Librarian adds, edits, or deletes books and papers in the resources DB.

threats.title: Librarian denies deleting a critical resource
threats.description: A librarian deletes an important digital resource from the library. Later, they claim they never did it. Because the system lacks a proper audit trail linking actions to specific user IDs, the university cannot prove who performed the deletion.
threats.mitigation: Ensure Process 3.0 sends a "Log Event" to D3 Audit Log containing the user ID, timestamp, and action performed.

data.name:
4.0 
Manage 
Users 
& 
Permissions
data.description: Admin creates, updates, deletes user accounts and changes roles. Handles credentials Handles PII

threats.title: Student manipulates account changes to gain Admin rights
threats.description: A student intercepts the "User account changes" data flow and modifies the request to change their own role from 'Student' to 'Administrator'. The server processes the request without checking if the requester has the authority to make that change.
threats.mitigation: Implement strict server-side Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Verify that the user making the request is an Admin before applying account updates.

data.name: D1 User Accounts
data.description: Stores usernames, hashed passwords, roles, and personal details.

threats.title: Direct database modification of user roles
threats.description: An attacker gains direct access to the D1 User Accounts database (e.g., via a misconfigured cloud port) and manually updates their account row to change their role to Administrator.
threats.mitigation: Restrict database access to only the application server's IP address, use strong database passwords, and encrypt the database at rest.

threats.title: Login floods lock up the user database
threats.description: An attacker sends thousands of concurrent login requests to Process 1.0. This causes Process 1.0 to open too many connections to D1 User Accounts, causing the database to crash and preventing all users from logging in.
threats.mitigation: Implement database connection pooling limits and configure rate limiting on the authentication endpoint.

data.name: D2 Digital Resources DB
data.description: Stores book/paper metadata, file paths, and resource records.

threats.title: Unencrypted database backup exposed
threats.description: An attacker gains access to the cloud storage where the Digital Resources DB is backed up. Because the backup is stored in plain text, the attacker downloads all copyrighted materials and restricted research papers.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt the database at rest and enforce strict access controls on cloud storage buckets.

threats.title: Attacker alters account permissions in transit
threats.description: An attacker intercepts the "User account changes" data flow using a Man-in-the-Middle attack. They modify the request payload to change a user's role from 'Student' to 'Administrator' before it reaches Process 4.0, granting them full control over the system.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt all internal data flows using TLS 1.3 to prevent interception, and implement server-side checksum validation to detect tampered payloads.

threats.title: SQL injection in the search query (Critical)
threats.description: A student enters malicious SQL code (e.g., ' OR 1=1 --) into the search query field. The application passes this input directly to D2 Digital Resources DB, allowing the attacker to dump the entire database.
threats.mitigation: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) for all database interactions and implement strict input validation.

threats.title: Malicious file intercepted and altered in transit
threats.description: A Man-in-the-Middle attacker intercepts the "Resource data" flow between the Librarian and Process 3.0. They alter the PDF file before it reaches the database, corrupting the integrity of the digital resource.
threats.mitigation: Enforce TLS 1.3 encryption for all data in transit and use file hashing to verify integrity upon receipt.

threats.title: Unauthorized reading of audit logs
threats.description: A curious student discovers that the D3 Audit Log is publicly accessible and reads the login history and IP addresses of other students and teachers.
threats.mitigation: Configure the audit log database with strict read-access controls so only the system administrator can view it.
